'''Mohammed Abdul Wazed Miah''' (6 February 1942 – 9 May 2009), locally known as, '''Sudha Mia,''' was a Bangladeshi physicist and the writer of a number of texts in physics and some political history books, a former chairman of the [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission]] and husband of former prime minister of Bangladesh [[Sheikh Hasina]].

==Early life==
Mohammed Abdul Wazed Miah was born on 16 February 1942 in the village of Fatehpur (Miah Bari) at [[Pirganj Upazila, Rangpur|Pirganj]], [[Rangpur District]] to Abdul Quader Miah and Moyzunnessa (Maijun Nesa Bibi).<ref name="Star">{{cite news|title=Life sketch of Wazed Miah|url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/newDesign/story.php?nid=87586|work=The Daily Star|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=15 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215113943/http://archive.thedailystar.net/newDesign/story.php?nid=87586|url-status=live}}</ref> He was the youngest among three sisters and four brothers. His uncle was Wazed Miah. He was then called 'Sudha Miah'.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wazed Mia's 80th birth anniv today |url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/162883/wazed-mias-80th-birth-anniv-today |access-date=16 February 2022 |work=New Age |language=en |archive-date=16 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216053957/https://www.newagebd.net/article/162883/wazed-mias-80th-birth-anniv-today |url-status=live }}</ref>

He passed the matriculation examination at [[Rangpur Zilla School]] in 1956, and earned his Intermediate Certificate at Rajshahi College in 1958.<ref name="Banglapedia">{{cite web |last1=Murshed |first1=Sanzida |title=Miah, MA Wazed |url=https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Miah,_MA_Wazed |website=Banglapedia}}</ref> He followed in the footsteps of his eldest sister's son, physicist <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bas.org.bd/index.php/fellow-details/40#:~:text=professor%20abdul%20qayyum%20sarker%20was%20born%20at%20rangpur%2C%20bangladesh%20in%201936 |title=Fellow Details - Bangladesh Academy of Sciences |website=bas.org.bd |access-date=10 November 2026}}</ref> Abdul Qayyum Sarker, and took admittance into the Department of Physics, [[University of Dhaka]]. In 1961 he graduated with a Bachelor of Science in [[physics]] and in 1962 he finished his Master of Science.<ref name="Star" /> He completed the Diploma of [[Imperial College London]] Course in 1963–64.<ref name="Star" /> In 1967 he received his Doctor of Philosophy degree in physics from [[Durham University]], England. His thesis was on the [[Bootstrap model|bootstrap hypothesis]] in theoretical particle physics, and he worked under Professor E. J. Squires.

===Student politics===
From 1961 to 1962, he was the vice-president of the [[Fazlul Huq Muslim Hall]] unit of the East Pakistan Muslim Chhatra League (now known as the [[Bangladesh Chhatra League]]) at the University of Dhaka. He was arrested for taking part in the [[1962 East Pakistan Education movement]] against Ayub's education commission. After university he did not remain involved in politics.<ref name="Banglapedia" />

==Career==

On 1 April 1963, Miah found employment with the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC), initially attached to the Atomic Energy Research Center (AERC) in Karachi.<ref name="Star" /> In 1969, Miah got an associateship at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Italy. In the same year, he returned home to Pakistan and continued with the AERC.<ref name="Star" /> In Karachi, Miah was the chief scientist at the [[Karachi Nuclear Power Plant]] but had his [[security clearance]] revoked, that led to termination of his contract and his migration to Bangladesh.{{rp|106}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Feroz |title=Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistani Bomb |date=7 November 2012 |publisher=Stanford University Press |isbn=978-0-8047-8480-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC&q=Eating+Grass%3A+The+Making+of+the+Pakistani+Bomb |access-date=25 February 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1975, he received advanced training in [[nuclear reactor physics]] in West Germany. His wife, [[Sheikh Hasina]], was with him, when her father, [[Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman|Prime Minister Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated]] along with most of his family.<ref name="Star" />

From 1975–1982 Wazed worked at the New Delhi-based laboratory of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India]] in exile with the remainder of the Mujib family after the bloody [[15 August 1975 Bangladesh coup d'état]]. After his return to Bangladesh, he joined the [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission]], and retired as its chairman in 1999.<ref name="Banglapedia" />

==Personal life and death==
On 17 November 1967, Miah married [[Sheikh Hasina]], eldest daughter of [[Sheikh Mujibur Rahman]], the founder of Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scientist Wazed Miah remembered|url=http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2014/05/09/scientist-wazed-miah-remembered|website=bdnews24.com|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=15 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215185102/http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2014/05/09/scientist-wazed-miah-remembered|url-status=live}}</ref> They have a son [[Sajeeb Wazed Joy]] and a daughter [[Saima Wazed Putul]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rangpur AL wants Joy to contest from Pirganj-6|url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/beta2/news/rangpur-al-wants-joy-to-contest-from-pirganj-6/|work=The Daily Star|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=15 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215113809/http://archive.thedailystar.net/beta2/news/rangpur-al-wants-joy-to-contest-from-pirganj-6/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Miah died on 9 May 2009, aged 67. He had for long suffered from [[Hypertension|high blood pressure]], [[Coronary artery disease|heart disease]], [[kidney failure]], [[Diabetes Mellitus|diabetes]], and [[asthma]]. He had a [[Coronary artery bypass graft|bypass operation]] a few years earlier and an [[angioplasty]] in Singapore only a few months before his death. He was buried at a family graveyard in his native village at [[Pirganj Upazila, Rangpur|Pirganj, Rangpur]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wazed Miah Is Dead|url=http://www.independent-bangladesh.com/2009050910944/country/wazed-miah-is-dead.html|website=independent-bangladesh.com|publisher=Bangladesh News|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=19 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220219042903/https://www.independent-bangladesh.com/|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Legacy==
One of the main science buildings of [[University of Rajshahi]], previously named as 4th Science Building, has been renamed after him as Dr. M Wazed Miah Academic Building and the [[Information and communications technology|Information and Communications Technology]] building of [[Shahjalal University of Science and Technology]] is named after him.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSE Carnival' begins at SUST|url=http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2015/11/27/cse-carnival-begins-at-sust|work=bdnews24.com|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=15 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151215030904/http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2015/11/27/cse-carnival-begins-at-sust|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, an academic building was constructed in his memory in [[Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hasina rejects BNP's formula|url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/beta2/news/hasina-rejects-bnps-formula/|work=The Daily Star|access-date=10 February 2016|archive-date=15 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215113820/http://archive.thedailystar.net/beta2/news/hasina-rejects-bnps-formula/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Publications==
* Fundamentals of Electro-Magnetics (1982)
* Fundamentals of Thermodynamics (University Press, Dhaka, 1988)
* Elementary Nuclear and Reactor Physics (1995)
* Basics of Superconductivity (1996)
* Some Thoughts on Science & Technology (1997)
* Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibke Ghire Kichhu Ghatana O Bangladesh [Some Events Centring Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib and Bangladesh] (1993)
* Bangladesher Rajniti O Sarkarer Chalchitra [Politics in Bangladesh and the Background Scenes of Governments] (1995)
* Bangladesher Bibhinna Somosyar Sombhabyo Somadhan [Probable Solutions of the Various Problems of Bangladesh] (1996)
